title: Bernice N. Waweru
text:
I’m a plant geneticist and bioinformatician working on disease resistance in wheat. For my PhD at the John Innes Centre and University of East Anglia, I developed k-mer and multi-reference genome methods to find and track resistance genes that standard reference genomes miss, particularly those carried by landraces and wild relatives. Applying these methods to the Yr47 yellow rust resistance locus from a Watkins landrace that remains resistant to newly emerged Yr15-virulent rust strains, I narrowed down candidate genes and developed diagnostic markers for breeders.
My work spans the field and the command line. Before my PhD, I spent seven years at KALRO in Kenya on wheat breeding and international rust screening, then worked as a bioinformatician at the BecA-ILRI Hub, contributing to genome assemblies for African orphan crops. I build reproducible analysis pipelines in Python, R and Nextflow on HPC, and gained industry breeding experience through PhD CASE placements at Limagrain and BASF.
I’m looking for roles where I can bring together genomics, genetics and breeding to address practical challenges in crop improvement and food security.
